title: Chips Spark a Catch-Up Rally in Seoul, but a 5% Yield Still Hangs Overhead
body:
Seoul stocks extended their rebound on Wednesday. The KOSPI rose 2.6% to 5,375.36, while the tech-heavy KOSDAQ jumped 5.6% to 705.10, which triggered a buy-side sidecar (프로그램 매매 일시 정지) for the second straight day. Foreign investors, who had been heavy sellers earlier this month, bought a net 655 billion won of shares, whereas individuals and institutions took profits.

Overnight, Wall Street **reinforced** the upbeat mood. Strong results from AI cloud provider CoreWeave **prompted** investors to return to chipmakers, sending the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 5.7%. The S&P 500 gained 1.3% to 7,619.38, and the Nasdaq added 1.6%, nearly erasing last week's AI-driven losses.

Even so, calling this a turning point would be premature. Although the KOSPI has climbed about 7% in just two sessions, it still sits 10.6% below its 20-day high, so it has **retraced** (되돌리다) only part of its recent slide. In fact, it is Korea that has **lagged behind**: over the past 20 trading days the KOSPI has lost 10.5%, compared with only 1.3% for the S&P 500. That gap suggests the move may be a **catch-up rally** rather than the start of a fresh uptrend. Meanwhile, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is hovering near 5.00%, a level that could **keep a lid on** expensive growth stocks. The longer yields stay there, the heavier that **overhang** (짓누르는 부담) will feel. If Applied Materials disappoints tonight, or if Nvidia falls short on November 17, the rally could fade as quickly as it began.
ko:
서울 증시가 수요일에도 반등을 이어갔다. 코스피는 2.6% 오른 5,375.36에 마감했고, 기술주 중심의 코스닥은 5.6% 급등한 705.10을 기록했는데, 이 때문에 이틀 연속 매수 사이드카가 발동됐다. 이달 초만 해도 대규모로 팔던 외국인은 6,552억 원어치를 순매수한 반면, 개인과 기관은 차익을 실현했다.

밤사이 월가는 이 분위기에 힘을 실었다. AI 클라우드 업체 코어위브의 호실적이 투자자들을 반도체주로 돌아오게 만들었고, 필라델피아 반도체지수는 5.7% 뛰었다. S&P500은 1.3% 오른 7,619.38, 나스닥은 1.6% 올라 지난주 AI발 하락분을 거의 되찾았다.

그렇다고 이것을 전환점이라 부르기는 이르다. 코스피가 단 두 거래일 만에 약 7% 올랐지만 여전히 20일 고점보다 10.6% 아래에 있어, 최근 하락분의 일부만 되돌린 셈이다. 사실 뒤처진 쪽은 바로 한국이다. 최근 20거래일 동안 코스피는 10.5% 하락했는데, S&P500은 1.3% 하락에 그쳤다. 이 격차는 이번 상승이 새로운 상승 추세의 시작이라기보다 '뒤따라잡기 반등'일 수 있음을 시사한다. 한편 미 10년물 국채금리는 5.00% 근처를 맴돌고 있는데, 이 수준은 비싼 성장주의 상승을 억누를 수 있다. 금리가 그 수준에 오래 머물수록 그 부담은 더 무겁게 느껴질 것이다. 오늘 밤 어플라이드 머티리얼즈가 실망을 주거나 11월 17일 엔비디아 실적이 기대에 못 미치면, 이번 반등은 시작만큼이나 빠르게 사그라들 수 있다.

vocab.en_easy: A rise in prices that happens because something fell behind others and is now closing the gap.
vocab.ex: Korean chip stocks staged a catch-up rally after the U.S. chip index jumped overnight.

vocab.en_easy: Something that hangs over the market and keeps prices from rising freely.
vocab.ex: High interest rates remain an overhang for growth stocks, even after a strong day.

vocab.en_easy: To move back over part of the way that a price has already gone.
vocab.ex: The index has retraced about half of last week's drop.

vocab.en_easy: To make an idea, feeling, or structure stronger.
vocab.ex: Running with a group every Saturday really reinforced my habit of exercising.

vocab.pos: v. (수능 빈출) — prompt + O + to V
vocab.en_easy: To cause someone to do something.
vocab.ex: The cold weather prompted me to switch from jogging outside to the treadmill.

vocab.en_easy: To move or develop more slowly than others.
vocab.ex: I used to lag behind the rest of my running crew, but now I can keep up.

vocab.en_easy: To control something so that it does not grow or get worse.
vocab.ex: I'm trying to keep a lid on my coffee spending — two cups a day, max.

grammar.point: 관계대명사 계속적 용법 (, which + 앞 절 전체 / 사람 + , who — that 은 계속적 용법 불가)
grammar.quote: …the tech-heavy KOSDAQ jumped 5.6% to 705.10, which triggered a buy-side sidecar… / Foreign investors, who had been heavy sellers earlier this month, bought…
grammar.explain_ko: 콤마 뒤 which 는 앞 절 전체('코스닥이 5.6% 뛴 일')를 받아 '그리고 그것이 ~했다'로 덧붙인다. 콤마 + who 는 이미 특정된 사람(외국인)에 대한 추가 정보. 계속적 용법에는 that 을 쓸 수 없다는 게 수능 어법 단골 포인트. (참고: 최근 14일 안에 16개 문법을 모두 한 번씩 써서, 가장 오래전(10/30)에 나온 항목을 다시 골랐다.)
examples: The stock jumped 10% in a day, which made me nervous rather than excited.
(OPIc) I go to a small gym near my office, which is open 24 hours, so I can work out even after a late night.

grammar.point: 비교급·최상급 응용 (The + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 … / as + 원급 + as)
grammar.quote: The longer yields stay there, the heavier that overhang will feel. / …the rally could fade as quickly as it began.
grammar.explain_ko: 'The 비교급 + 주어 + 동사, the 비교급 + 주어 + 동사' = ~할수록 더 …하다. 두 번째 절은 미래(will)여도 첫 절은 현재시제. as quickly as 는 동사 fade 를 꾸미니까 부사 quickly — 형용사 quick 을 쓰면 어법 오류.
examples: The more you trade on emotion, the more you tend to lose.
(OPIc) The colder it gets, the harder it is for me to get out of bed for my morning run.

tense.sentence: Although the KOSPI has climbed about 7% in just two sessions, it still sits 10.6% below its 20-day high.
tense.why_ko: '두 거래일 동안 올라서 지금 이 상태'라는 과거→현재 연결. 특정 과거 시점(on Wednesday)이 없으니 현재완료.

tense.sentence: Foreign investors, who had been heavy sellers earlier this month, bought a net 655 billion won of shares.
tense.why_ko: 수요일에 '샀다(bought)'는 기준 과거보다 '그 전에 팔고 있었다'가 더 앞선 일이라 had been.

review.q:
빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 표현은?
"Nvidia doesn't report until next Tuesday, so loading up on chip stocks today would be ______."
review.exp_ko: jump the gun = (신호 전에) 너무 서두르다 → 실적 발표 전 미리 사는 상황(①). ② 하룻밤 생각해 보기(오히려 반대 행동) ③ 열기가 식다(주어가 시장일 때) ④ 한곳에 진 치고 머물다 — 문맥상 '성급함'이 아니다.

review.q:
밑줄 친 부분과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
"I wouldn't read too much into a two-day bounce."
choices: I wouldn't sell stocks during a two-day bounce.
I wouldn't pay any attention to a two-day bounce.
I wouldn't predict how long a two-day bounce lasts.
I wouldn't give a two-day bounce more meaning than it deserves.
review.exp_ko: read too much into = 실제보다 큰 의미를 부여하다(④). ② '아예 무시하다'는 지나친 해석 — 원문은 보긴 보되 과대해석하지 말라는 뜻. ① 매도 ③ 기간 예측은 원문에 없는 행동.

review.q:
빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 표현은?
"After two days of sidecars in a row, I'm going to ______ before I put any new money in."
review.exp_ko: let the dust settle = 소란이 가라앉길 기다리다(③). ① 오르는 장을 쫓아 사다(반대 행동) ② 순식간에 방향을 바꾸다 ④ 빈둥거리다(일상 표현, 투자 문맥 X).

quiz.q:
[어휘·문맥] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Strong results from AI cloud provider CoreWeave ______ investors to return to chipmakers."
quiz.exp_ko: '목적어(investors) + to V'를 바로 받을 수 있는 동사는 prompt(~하게 만들다)뿐(②). ① account for ③ result in ④ contribute to 는 모두 '원인·결과'를 말하지만 전치사가 필요하고 O + to V 구조를 못 받는다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"①The heavier the overhang becomes, the slower the index recovers. A rally can fade ②as quickly as it begins. The KOSDAQ jumped 5.6%, ③which triggered a sidecar. Foreign investors, ④that had been heavy sellers, turned into buyers."
quiz.exp_ko: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법에는 that 을 쓸 수 없다 → who 가 맞다(④). ① The 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ✓ ② 동사 fade 수식이라 부사 quickly ✓ ③ 앞 절 전체를 받는 계속적 용법 which ✓.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: ① The two-day jump looks more like a catch-up move than a confirmed turn, as high yields and chip earnings still loom.
② Heavy foreign buying shows that the Korean market has already recovered all of its losses from last month.
③ Korean stocks have outperformed U.S. stocks over the past month, so further gains in Seoul are likely.
④ Rising Treasury yields were the main reason chip stocks surged on Wall Street during the overnight session.
quiz.exp_ko: 본문은 '반등은 강했다 → 그러나(Even so) 20일 고점 아래·한국은 뒤처짐·금리 부담·실적 이벤트' 구조로, 반등을 추세 전환으로 단정하지 말라는 게 요지(①). ② 고점 대비 −10.6%라 '전부 회복'은 틀림 ③ 20일간 코스피 −10.5% vs S&P −1.3%로 반대 ④ 반도체 급등 원인은 코어위브 실적, 금리는 오히려 부담 요인.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 수치로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: ① On Wednesday, the KOSDAQ's percentage gain was more than three times the KOSPI's.
② The KOSPI's two-day gain was larger than its remaining distance from the 20-day high.
③ Over 20 trading days, the KOSPI's decline was roughly eight times as large as the S&P 500's.
④ Overnight, the chip index rose more than four times as much as the Nasdaq in percentage terms.
quiz.exp_ko: 10.5 ÷ 1.3 ≈ 8.1배 → ③ 정답. ① 5.6 ÷ 2.6 ≈ 2.2배(3배 미만) ② 이틀 상승 약 7% < 고점까지 10.6% ④ 5.7 ÷ 1.6 ≈ 3.6배(4배 미만) — 모두 숫자 두 개를 나눠 봐야 걸러진다.

talk.topic: Two days, +7% — 코스피 뒤따라잡기 반등인가, 바닥인가 (옵션 만기·AMAT 실적 D-day)
talk.setting_ko: 목요일 아침 출근길, 회사 동료 둘이 이틀 연속 사이드카 뒤 시장 얘기를 한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see the KOSDAQ? Another sidecar. That's two days in a row.
dialogue.ko: 코스닥 봤어? 또 사이드카야. 이틀 연속이라고.

dialogue.en: Yeah, chips are on a roll. The U.S. chip index was up almost six percent last night.
dialogue.ko: 응, 반도체가 연승 행진이야. 어젯밤 미국 반도체지수가 거의 6% 올랐잖아.

dialogue.en: So is this the bottom? I'm kind of having second thoughts about the cash I've been sitting on.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이게 바닥이야? 쥐고 있던 현금, 계속 들고 있을지 좀 다시 생각하게 되네.

dialogue.en: I wouldn't bet the farm on it. The KOSPI's still more than ten percent off its recent high.
dialogue.ko: 나라면 올인은 안 해. 코스피는 아직 최근 고점보다 10% 넘게 아래야.

dialogue.en: True. And yields are still sitting around five percent.
Exactly. The real test is Nvidia next week. If that goes well, then maybe.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 진짜 시험대는 다음 주 엔비디아야. 그게 잘 나오면 그땐 몰라도.

dialogue.en: Buying in small pieces until then sounds smart, but that's easier said than done when everything's green.
dialogue.ko: 그때까지 조금씩 나눠 사는 게 현명하긴 한데, 다 빨간불(상승)일 땐 말처럼 쉽지가 않지.

dialogue.en: Ha, tell me about it. Let's just stick to small orders and see how today's options expiry plays out.
dialogue.ko: 하, 내 말이. 일단 소액 주문만 하고 오늘 옵션 만기가 어떻게 흘러가는지 보자.

expressions.ex: I've hit the gym five days straight — I'm on a roll.
I'm having second thoughts about signing up for the full marathon.

expressions.en: I wouldn't bet the farm on it.
expressions.when_ko: 가능성은 있지만 확신은 없다고 말할 때
expressions.ex: The rebound might continue, but I wouldn't bet the farm on it.

expressions.when_ko: 앞으로 결과를 가를 핵심 이벤트를 짚을 때
expressions.ex: The real test is whether I can keep running when it gets below zero.
'Just don't check your account every hour' — that's easier said than done.

your_turn.q_en: After two big up days in a row, would you add more money now or wait for a specific event? Explain why.
your_turn.hint_ko: 입장 1문장 → 이유 2개(고점까지 남은 거리·금리/실적 이벤트) → the 비교급, the 비교급 한 번 → 마무리 계획(분할 매수 등)
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I'd wait, or at least go slowly. Two days of sidecars feel exciting, but the index is still more than ten percent below its recent high, so it might just be a catch-up rally. The real test is Nvidia next week. The bigger the rally gets before that, the more careful I want to be. So I'll split my orders into small pieces, which helps me avoid buying everything at the top.

talk.topic: 추워진 아침, 러닝크루 첫 참여 — 페이스 조절과 옆구리 통증 (Background Survey #46 조깅)
talk.setting_ko: 토요일 아침 한강공원. 겸이가 친구 소개로 동네 러닝크루에 처음 나왔다.

dialogue.en: Hey, you made it! Welcome to the crew. It's freezing today, huh?
dialogue.ko: 오, 왔네! 크루에 온 걸 환영해. 오늘 엄청 춥다, 그치?

dialogue.en: Tell me about it. I almost stayed in bed. How fast do you guys usually go?
dialogue.ko: 그러게. 이불 밖에 안 나올 뻔했어. 보통 얼마나 빨리 달려?

dialogue.en: Around six minutes per kilometer. Just pace yourself and you'll be fine.
dialogue.ko: 킬로미터당 6분 정도. 페이스만 잘 조절하면 괜찮을 거야.

dialogue.en: I'll try to keep up with you, but no promises.
dialogue.ko: 따라가 볼게, 근데 장담은 못 해.

dialogue.en: (20 minutes later) You okay? You're holding your side.
I've got a stitch. I think I started out way too fast.
dialogue.ko: 옆구리가 결려. 처음에 너무 빨리 나간 것 같아.

dialogue.en: Slow down and breathe deeply. Push through the last kilometer and we'll grab coffee.
dialogue.ko: 속도 줄이고 깊게 숨 쉬어. 마지막 1km만 버티면 커피 마시러 가자.

dialogue.en: Deal. But after that, I'm totally beat.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 근데 끝나면 나 완전 녹초야.

expressions.ex: It's a long hike, so pace yourself in the first hour.
It's hard to keep up with all the new songs these days.

expressions.when_ko: 달리기 중 옆구리 통증을 말할 때
expressions.ex: I always get a stitch if I run right after lunch.
My legs were burning, but I pushed through the last set of squats.
After that 10K, I'm totally beat — I need a nap.

your_turn.q_en: Have you ever exercised with a group or a club? How was it different from exercising alone?
your_turn.hint_ko: 경험 1개(언제·어디·누구) → 혼자 vs 같이 차이 2개(페이스·동기) → 오늘 표현 2개(pace myself, keep up with) → 마무리 소감
your_turn.sample_answer: Yeah, I actually joined a running crew by the Han River last weekend. When I run alone, I usually go at my own speed and stop whenever I want. With the crew, though, I had to keep up with people who were way faster than me, so I got a stitch about twenty minutes in. Still, I pushed through, and finishing together felt amazing. The more people I run with, the less I want to quit, I guess.

opic.survey_topic: 목요일 돌발 주제 — 기술·AI (서베이 #31 주식 투자 · #23 음악 감상 · #51 헬스와 연결)

combo.q_en: I'd like to talk about technology. These days, many people use different kinds of technology in their daily lives. What kinds of technology do people in your country use most often? Tell me about them in detail.
combo.q_ko: 기술에 대해 이야기해 보죠. 요즘 많은 사람들이 일상에서 다양한 기술을 씁니다. 당신 나라 사람들이 가장 자주 쓰는 기술은 무엇인가요? 자세히 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(한국 = 스마트폰 없이는 하루도 못 사는 나라, 한 줄) → 본문 ① 스마트폰 앱(지하철·결제·배달) ② AI 도구(번역·요약·음악 추천) ③ 내 경우(주식 앱·운동 기록 앱) — 각 포인트에 구체적 예 1개 → 마무리(편리하지만 너무 의존한다는 생각). 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: 일반론(people in Korea) → 나(I) 로 좁히는 문단 구조, 현재시제 일관, which 계속적 용법 1번.
combo.model_answer: Oh, technology? Well, in Korea, I'd say smartphones are basically part of your body. I mean, you can't really get through a day without one. First of all, people use their phones for pretty much everything — paying for coffee, checking when the next subway is coming, ordering food, you name it. Even street vendors take mobile payments now, which is kind of amazing if you think about it. And these days, AI tools are getting really popular. A lot of my coworkers use AI to summarize long reports or translate emails. As for me, I use a music app that recommends songs based on what I listen to, and honestly, it knows my taste better than my friends do. Oh, and I also check a stock app every morning and use a fitness app to track my workouts — like how much I lifted on leg day. So, yeah, technology makes life super convenient. But sometimes I feel like we depend on it a little too much, you know? When my phone dies, I literally feel lost.

key_phrases.en: ~ is basically part of your body
we depend on it a little too much

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '앱을 많이 쓴다'에서 끝난다. IH는 사회 일반 → 내 사례로 좁히고, AL은 마지막에 '편리함 vs 의존'처럼 자기 의견(평가)까지 붙인다.

combo.q_en: How has technology changed over the years? Compare the technology people used when you were growing up with the technology people use today. What are the biggest differences?
combo.q_ko: 기술은 수년간 어떻게 변해 왔나요? 당신이 자랄 때 사람들이 쓰던 기술과 오늘날 쓰는 기술을 비교해 주세요. 가장 큰 차이는 무엇인가요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(차이가 엄청 크다 한 줄) → 본문 ① 과거(used to + 동사원형: 폴더폰·MP3·PC방) ② 현재(현재시제: 스마트폰 하나로 전부·AI) ③ 가장 큰 차이 1개(속도·편리함) + 장단점 → 마무리(앞으로 더 빨라질 것 — will). 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거-현재-미래 시제 전환이 정확한지, the 비교급 the 비교급 한 번, 'Back then / Nowadays' 대비 연결어.
combo.model_answer: Wow, technology has changed so much. Let me think. When I was in middle school, I used to carry around a flip phone and a separate MP3 player. I had to download songs on my computer, put them on the MP3 player, and if I wanted new music, I had to do the whole thing again. It was kind of a pain, actually. And if you wanted to look something up, you had to sit in front of a desktop. Nowadays, though, everything is in one device. I can stream any song, check my stocks, and even ask an AI to plan my workout, all from my phone. I think the biggest difference is speed. Things that used to take an hour now take, like, ten seconds. But here's the thing — the faster technology gets, the shorter our attention span seems to get. I mean, I can't even watch a whole movie without checking my phone. Anyway, I'm pretty sure it'll keep changing even faster in the next ten years.

key_phrases.en: It was kind of a pain.
Things that used to take ~ now take ~
the faster ~ gets, the shorter ~ gets

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 과거/현재를 따로 나열한다. IH는 used to ↔ nowadays 로 같은 항목(음악 듣는 방식)을 직접 대비하고, AL은 'the 비교급, the 비교급'으로 변화의 부작용까지 한 문장에 묶는다.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a time when you had a problem with a piece of technology. What happened, and how did you deal with it? Please tell me everything from beginning to end.
combo.q_ko: 기술 기기 때문에 문제를 겪었던 때를 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했나요? 처음부터 끝까지 전부 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디서 — '작년 이맘때, 장 열리기 직전') → 본문 ① 사건 발생(과거시제, 긴장감: 앱이 멈춤) ② 해결 시도 2단계(재시작 → PC/고객센터) ③ 결과와 감정 → 마무리(그 뒤로 바뀐 습관 — now I always ~). 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거시제 일관 + 과거완료 1번(had already ~), 대사 인용('I was like, ~'), 자기수정(Actually, no — it was ~).
combo.model_answer: Oh, I remember this one really clearly. It was last year, on a day when the market was going crazy. I had planned to sell some shares right at the opening bell, but when I opened my stock app, it just froze. The screen was stuck on the loading page. I was like, 'Are you kidding me? Not today!' So first, I restarted my phone, but it didn't help. Then I tried logging in on my laptop, and — actually, no, wait — I think I tried my company computer first, which was a bad idea because it was blocked. Anyway, by the time I finally got into the system through the website, the price had already dropped about three percent. I was so frustrated. I called the customer center, and they said a lot of people had the same problem that morning because of heavy traffic. Looking back, it was a good lesson, though. Now I always keep the app and the website open on two devices on big market days, just in case.

key_phrases.en: I remember this one really clearly.
I was like, 'Are you kidding me?'
by the time I ~, it had already ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '앱이 멈췄다, 고쳤다'로 끝난다. IH는 시도→실패→해결 순서를 시간 연결어로 잇고, AL은 자기수정(actually, no, wait)과 by the time + 과거완료로 '사건의 순서'를 정확히 보여 준다.

aptitude.q: 코스닥 지수는 11월 10일 667.61에서 11월 11일 705.10으로 올랐다. 11월 11일 코스닥의 전일 대비 상승률은? (가장 가까운 값)
코스피는 11월 10일 +4.4%, 11월 11일 +2.6% 올라 11월 11일 5,375.36으로 마감했다. 11월 9일 종가는 약 얼마인가? (일별 상승률만 이용, 가장 가까운 값)
11월 11일 코스피에서 외국인은 6,552억 원을 순매수했고, 기관은 4,824억 원, 개인은 7,155억 원을 순매도했다. 기관·개인 순매도 합계에서 개인이 차지하는 비중은? (가장 가까운 값)
aptitude.exp_ko: ① 분모 동그라미: '기관·개인 순매도 합계에서' → 분모 = 4,824 + 7,155 = 11,979. ② 쉬운 수로: 11,979 → 12,000. ③ 1% = 120 → 7,155 ÷ 120 ≈ 59.6 → 분모를 살짝 키웠으니 실제는 조금 크다 → 59.7%. ④ 거꾸로 검산: 11,979 × 60% = 7,187, 0.3%(36)를 빼면 7,151 ≈ 7,155 ✓ / 52.2%면 6,253으로 900 부족 ✗. 함정: ① 40.3%는 기관 비중(방향 반대), ② 52.2%는 분모에 외국인을 넣은 값, ⑤ 148.3%는 개인 ÷ 기관(분모 바꿔치기), ④ 109.2%는 개인 ÷ 외국인. 개인이 기관보다 크니 50~100% 사이 보기 중에서 고르면 2개로 좁혀진다.
